BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE VIVEK RUSIA  ON THE 10th OF SEPTEMBER, 2024  WRIT PETITION No. 16972 of 2011  SYED IMDAD HUSSAIN AND OTHERS  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Sanjay Agrawal, Senior Advocate alongwith Yash Soni, le  for the petitioner.
 Shri Abhijeet Awasthi, Deputy Advocate General for the respo  ORDER Petitioners have filed the present Writ Petition challenging the order dated 29.08.2011 passed by the respondent No.2 whereby the representation of the petitioners has been rejected submitted for grant of land in lieu of monetary compensation payable under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
Facts of the case in short are as under;-
2.
The petitioner No.1 and petitioner No.2 are husband and wife.
The petitioner No.3 is power of attorney holder of petitioner No.1 and petitioner No.2.

the petitioner No.1 was owner of land bearing Khasra No.535/2, 536/3, 539/3, 617/535/2 having an area 0.227, 0.036, 1.509 and 0.142 hectares respectively, total 1.914 hectares situated in Village Barkheda Bondar, Tahsil Huzur, District Bhopal.
Likewise, the petitioner No.2 also has her land bearing Khasra Nos.246, 249-250, 255 and 262/1 having an area 2.63, 0.770, 1.02 and 2.84 hectares respectively total area 4.705 hectares.

Sajjad Hussain has sold the aforesaid land to the petitioner No.2 by a registered sale-deed dated 28.08.2006.
4.
The petitioner No.3 had also his land bearing khasra No.428/1 and 439 area being 0.255 and 0.251 hectares respectively making a total of 0.506 hectares in village Barkheda Bondar.
The petitioner No.3 has executed a power of attorney in favour of Syed Javed Ahmed, son of the petitioner No.1 authorizing him to do all acts on his behalf.

5. The Executive Engineer, Public Works Department sent a request letter dated 08.08.2006 to the State Government for acquisition of land admeasuring 89.45 hectares situated in Village Barkheda Bondar and 18.953 hectares situated in Village Mirpur, total 108.404 hectares for Defence Department to be used for extension of Aerodrum at Bhopal.
In pursuant to the aforesaid letter, a notification under Section 4(1) read with Section 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was issued.

Thereafter, subsequent notifications were issued time to time and after following due process of law,
award dated 18.12.2006 was passed for payment of compensation to the land owners.

6. The petitioner submitted an application to the Collector (Land Acquisition) on 26.07.2007 and to the Land Acquisition Officer, Bhopal on 10.04.2008 for allotment of any government land in lieu of monetary compensation.

The Naib Tehsildar, Tahsil Huzur, District Bhopal called a NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:45707 3 WP-16972-2011 report from the concerned Patwari and according to which the petitioners did not receive monetary compensation from the Government.
According to the petitioners, total 42.84 hectares land is available in the Village Bansiya, Tahsil Huzur, District Bhopal and that could be allotted to them in lieu of monetary compensation.

The application of the petitioners was not considered and rejected on 03.02.2010 on the ground that there is no provision in the Land Acquisition Act for allotment of land in lieu of monetary compensation.

The petitioners approached before this Court by way of Writ Petition No. 3724/2011 inter alia on the ground that there is specific provision under Section 31(3) of Land Acquisition Act,
1894 for grant of land in place of monetary compensation.

Vide order dated 08.03.2011, the order of Collector was set aside and matter was sent back to Collector to decide the application of the petitioners on the touch stone and anvil of the provision of Section 31(3) of the Act.

The petitioners submitted detailed representation on 25.03.2011 which came to be rejected by the Collector vide order dated 29.08.2011 only on the ground that various government projects are pending for consideration for which the government land would be required in future, therefore, the application of the petitioner cannot be considered, hence, the petitioner approached before this Court by way of present Writ Petition.

7. Shri Sanjay Agrawal, learned Senior counsel appearing on behalf of petitioners submits that earlier the Collector had wrongly rejected the application on the ground that there is no provision under the Land Acquisition Act for grant of land in lieu of monetary compensation and now NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:45707 4 WP-16972-2011 when the Section 31(3) of the Act brought into the notice to him, the claim of the petitioners has been rejected on imaginary ground that certain projects are pending for which the land would be required, however, no details of any project has been given.

It is further submitted that till today the petitioners have not accepted the monetary compensation from the respondents, therefore, the proceedings cannot be said to be Syed Imdad Hussain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131454187/

sentences.text: 2 concluded under the provision of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 therefore, the respondents be directed to allot any vacant government land to the petitioners so that they can earn their livelihood.

8. Learned Deputy Advocate General appearing on behalf of respondents submits that Section 31 of the Act is not in a nature of mandatory provision under which the petitioners' claim allotment of the land in place of monetary compensation is liable to be allowed.

It is purely a discretion of Government to consider the such request subject to availability of the vacant land for allotment to the land owners, therefore no interference is called for and Writ Petition is liable to be dismissed.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire documents available with the file.
9. The facts stated in above paras are not in dispute in this case, in respect of acquisition of land and passing of award dated 18.12.2006 by Land Acquisition Officer.
The entire claim of the petitioners is based on interpretation of Section 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

For the ready reference,
same is reproduced below;-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:45707 5 WP-16972-2011 ''31. Payment of compensation or deposit of same in Court .(1)

On making an award under section 11, the Collector shall tender payment of the compen- sation awarded by him to the persons interested entitled thereto according to the award and shall pay it to them unless prevented by some one or more of the contingencies mentioned in the next sub-section.

(2) If they shall not consent to receive it, or if there be no person competent to alienate the land, or if there be any dispute as to the title to receive the compensation or as to the apportionment of it, the Collector shall deposit the amount of the compensation in the Court to which a reference under section 18 would be submitted:
Provided that any person admitted to be interested may receive such payment under protest as to the sufficiency of the amount:
Provided also that no person who has received the amount otherwise than under protest shall be entitled to make any application under section 18:
Provided also that nothing herein contained shall affect the liability of any person,
who may receive the whole or any part of any compensation awarded under this Act,
to pay the same to the person lawfully entitled NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:45707 6 WP-16972-2011 thereto.

(3) Notwithstanding anything in this section, the Collector may, with the sanction of the [appropriate Government] instead of awarding a money compensation in respect of any land, make any arrangement with a person having a limited interest in such land, either by the grant of other lands in exchange, the remission of land revenue on other lands held under the same title, or in such other way as may be equitable having regard to the interests of the parties concerned.

3 (4) Nothing in the last foregoing sub-section shall be construed to interfere with or limit the power of the Collector to enter into any arrangement with any person interested in the land and competent to contract in respect thereof.''

sentences.text: From the plain language of the aforesaid section, it is clear that the Collector ''may'' with the prior sanction of appropriate Government instead of awarding a money compensation in respect of such land, make any arrangement with a person having a limited interest in such land, either by the grant of other lands in exchange.

Therefore, the Collector is liable to take decision for allotment of any other land during the assessment proceedings for awarding monetary compensation at the time of passing the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:45707 7 WP-16972-2011 award.
In the present case, the award was passed on 18.12.2006 and after seven months, the petitioners moved an application before the Collector for allotment of the land.

It is settled law that after passing of the award, same become final unless an application under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act is filed for seeking reference before the District Court only for purpose of enhancement of compensation.
After passing the award, the Collector becomes functus officio and not authorized to entertain any application to modify the award.

The Land Acquisition Officer passed an award in respect of allotment of the land in place of monetary compensation than before the Collector for its approval and after approval of the Collector, it becomes final award for distribution of the compensation,
therefore, the award had become final on 18.12.2006, thereafter, the petitioners filed an application for allotment of land.
The Land Acquisition Officer or the Collector is required to consider the prayer of the land owners for grant of land in place of compensation at that stage.
11. Even otherwise, Section 31(3) of the Act, it is not mandatory or obligatory on part of the Collector to allotment of land in place of land acquisition on request of land owners.

The word 'may' is used,
therefore, no writ of mandamus can be issued to the Collector for allotment of land.

Even otherwise,
now the Land Acquisition Act has been replaced by the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (RFCTLARR) Act, 2013 w.e.f.
01.04.2014.
